renders._yaml:
- component: card
  id: quality_tiers
  title: Sequences by quality tier
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of viral sequences assessed, and the bar splits them by CheckV quality tier. It answers how much of the viral content is usable.
    How to read: complete and high-quality sequences are ready for analysis. Medium and low-quality ones are partial genomes, and undetermined ones could not be given a tier. Tiers rest on completeness alone.
    Source: https://bitbucket.org/berkeleylab/checkv/raw/master/README.md
  column: contig_length
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: checkv_quality
  caption: sequences, by CheckV tier
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: completeness
  title: Completeness
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median estimated completeness of the sequences, in percent, and the bar compares it with the quality tiers. It answers how much of a full genome the sequences cover.
    How to read: a median above the high-quality floor means most sequences are near-complete genomes. A low median with a wide minimum to maximum spread points to many fragments, so check the scatter for which sequences pull it down.
    Lines and annotations: CheckV calls a sequence high-quality above 90% completeness and medium-quality between 50% and 90%, so the marks sit at 90 and 50.
    Source: https://bitbucket.org/berkeleylab/checkv/raw/master/README.md
  column: completeness
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 90.0
  threshold_direction: min
  threshold_warn: 50.0
  caption: median against the 90% high-quality floor

- component: card
  id: contamination
  title: Host contamination
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest estimated host contamination of any sequence, in percent, with the mean beside it, and the histogram shows how it is distributed. It answers whether proviruses carry host sequence at their edges.
    How to read: a long tail points to proviruses with host flanks. CheckV does not use contamination in its tiers, because host sequence is easy to trim, so no cut-off is drawn.
    Source: https://bitbucket.org/berkeleylab/checkv/raw/master/README.md
  column: contamination
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - average
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: contamination, per sequence

- component: advanced_viz
  id: completeness_vs_contamination
  title: Completeness against contamination
  description: |-
    Each point is a viral sequence: its estimated completeness on the horizontal axis and its host contamination on the vertical axis, sized by sequence length and coloured by quality tier. It answers which sequences are complete and clean.
    How to read: complete genomes sit at the right with no contamination, while proviruses with host flanks rise on the vertical axis. Fragments sit to the left, and large points are the longer sequences.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical line is 90% completeness, the floor of CheckV's high-quality tier.
    Source: https://bitbucket.org/berkeleylab/checkv/raw/master/README.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Estimated completeness (%)
    y_title: Estimated host contamination (%)
    reference_line: vertical
    reference_value: 90
    reference_label: 90% completeness (high-quality tier)
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    x: completeness
    y: contamination
    label: contig_id
    color: checkv_quality
    size: contig_length

- component: table
  title: Viral sequence quality
  description: |-
    Each row is a viral sequence with its length, provirus call, gene counts, completeness, contamination, quality tier and warnings. It answers which sequences to keep.
    How to read: sort by completeness and read the warnings column before trusting a high-quality call.
